questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?

options.text: Left
Right
Center

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always bad. Good riders change position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center position is probably the safest.

questions.question: What happens if you lock your brakes?

options.text: Be helpful in most situations.
Improve steering.
Cause control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on good pavement when stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Speed up.
Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, you should make sure it:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is clean.
Looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives the best protection when it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible damage.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They provide better grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They provide better grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you better grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong, durable material.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to ride right after rain starts?

options.text: Some other drivers may not react quickly enough to the rain.
The pavement becomes especially slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement becomes especially slippery.
questions.explanation: Pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, creating a slippery mixture with water.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Drivers must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows them to turn in their desired direction.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection when riding. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding skills. If you drink any amount of alcohol, it is not safe to ride.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: Having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can be impaired after your first drink. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection with no traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at the same time.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly when:

options.text: Your fingertips barely touch the handlebars while you are seated.
The seat is about one foot higher than your waist when you stand next to it.
Your feet touch the ground comfortably when you are seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet touch the ground comfortably when you are seated.
questions.explanation: Your feet should reach the ground comfortably while seated. Make sure the motorcycle fits you before you ride it.

questions.question: To stop a motorcycle quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together for a quick stop. Look ahead on the road to help you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
You see air being released.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways side to side.
questions.explanation: A flat rear tire may cause the back of the motorcycle to jerk or sway. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not change gears.
Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the transmission should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when in neutral.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle ride is to:

options.text: Take frequent rest breaks.
Ride as fast as possible.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Limit your daily riding time and take frequent rest breaks to avoid fatigue. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may crash from extreme fatigue when they wear off.
